Definition: to swell up (literally or figuratively, active or passive); by implication, to favor or honour, be high or proud
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hâdar where we would say to honour, to favour; to swell with pride. In Leviticus 19:15, the text says "nor honour the person of the mighty." The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hâdar this way, I believe pride is the oldest sin, and it always ends the same way — brought low. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
